name: Prakrit (Southern Epigraphical)
linguisticFeatures: Middle Indo-Aryan vernaculars (Maharashtri/Sauraseni derivatives) exhibiting consonant assimilation (e.g. dharma -> dhamma), absence of complex consonant clusters, and simplified case inflections.
description: Used predominantly in Mauryan rock edicts (Maski, Brahmagiri, Siddapura) and Satavahana inscriptions. Represents the earliest documented administrative and religious epigraphical language in Karnataka prior to the epigraphical emergence of classical Kannada.

name: Sanskrit (Epigraphical Classical)
linguisticFeatures: Standard Paninian grammatical structure, elaborate nominal compounds (Samasa), invocatory metric verses (Shlokas), and royal Prashasti genealogical eulogies chiseled in Kannada script.
description: The pan-Indian liturgical and courtly prestige language extensively employed across royal charters by Kadamba, Badami Chalukya, Rashtrakuta, and Vijayanagara sovereigns, frequently written in regional Kannada-Brahmi script.

name: Purvada Halegannada (Proto-Old Kannada)
linguisticFeatures: Transitional archaic Dravidian morphology; retention of Sakata Repha (ಱ) and retroflex liquid (ೞ); vowel harmony; primitive case markers; Sanskrit loan vocabulary integrated with native verbal roots without Dravidian gender inflection normalization.
description: The foundational linguistic phase of the Kannada language attested on monumental stones such as the Halmidi Inscription (c. 450 CE). Represents the direct precursor to classical Old Kannada literature.

name: Halegannada (Classical Old Kannada)
linguisticFeatures: Highly standardized literary grammatical canons formulated in Kavirajamarga; strict adherence to native Champu poetic metres (Kanda, Vritta, Tripadi); complex case terminations (-am, -im, -ke); phonetic differentiation of ಱ and ೞ.
description: The golden age of Kannada epigraphy and literature under the Rashtrakutas, Western Chalukyas, and Hoysalas. Celebrated in thousands of poetic steles across Karnataka by court poets like Pampa, Ranna, and Ravikirti.

name: Nadugannada (Middle Kannada)
linguisticFeatures: Systematic phonological transition of initial 'P' to 'H' (e.g. palu -> halu, piri -> hiriya); merger of archaic liquid ೞ into ḷ or r; emergence of Shatpadi and Sangatya metric meters; democratization of language via Sharana Vachana literature.
description: The language of the Bhakti movement, Vijayanagara administration, and popular epic poetry (Kumaravyasa Bharata), exhibiting direct morphological continuities with Modern Standard Kannada.

name: Hosagannada (Modern Standard Kannada)
linguisticFeatures: Complete consolidation of 'H' for historical 'P'; loss of case suffix gemination; streamlined syntactic word order (Subject-Object-Verb); normalized typographic standard in modern print and digital media.
description: The contemporary standardized literary and administrative language of the state of Karnataka, spoken by over 50 million people and codified in the official Unicode Kannada block (U+0C80–U+0CFF).
